keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Montenegro shape begins in 1853, but the principality was created on 13 March 1852 ('Danilo I Petrovic-Njegos gave up his position as prince-bishop and married'). The 1853 shape is used unchanged for 1852; the page gives no 1852 area beyond '4,405 km2' before the growth of 1878.

6,131.5 km2 against the page's 4,405 km2 for the principality before 1878 (ratio 1.39, inside a factor of two). Grahovo, Rudine and other areas were gained after the Battle of Grahovac (May 1858), which the shape probably includes since it cannot be split. The shape should end in 1877: the gains of 1878 follow the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878), not 1880 or 1885.

Ulcinj's handover is not on the pages opened, so its date inside 1878-1885 is open.

8,793.6 km2, ratio 0.93 against the page's 9,475 km2. Shape right; Cliopatria starts it in 1885 but the Treaty of Berlin (signed 13 July 1878) recognised the independence and the growth dates from 1878.

Unverified: page budget. 9,030.9 km2 (+237 km2 on 1910); nothing on the pages opened explains the small change. The kingdom was proclaimed on 28 August 1910 ('Prince Nikola of Montenegro proclaimed the Kingdom of Montenegro in Cetinje on 28 August 1910').

region.text: the principality created when Danilo I gave up his position as prince-bishop (Cetinje)

ledger.note: 13 March 1852: Danilo I secularises the prince-bishopric and Montenegro becomes a principality. 'Danilo I Petrovic-Njegos gave up his position as prince-bishop and married, which created the principality.' The page gives no frontier; the core is Cliopatria's 1853 shape. Capital Cetinje.

region.text: Grahovo and the Rudine, gained after the Battle of Grahovac

ledger.note: May 1858: Montenegro wins at Grahovac and the border is redrawn. 'Battle of Grahovac, May 1858: Mirko Petrovic's army defeated the Ottoman forces' (13 May in the text, 1 May in the infobox); the Great Powers then demarcated the border and Montenegro gained Grahovo, Rudine and other areas. The date of the demarcation is not on the page, and the text also lists Niksic, which Cliopatria draws only from 1885.

region.text: the Ottoman districts around Niksic, Podgorica, Bar and Kolasin that Montenegro took in 1876-78

ledger.note: July 1876: the Montenegrin-Ottoman War opens. 'Battle of Vucji Do (18 July 1876) and the Montenegrin-Ottoman War (1876-78), which followed Nikola's support for the Herzegovina Uprising (1875-78).'
13 July 1878: the Treaty of Berlin ends the war. 'The treaty was signed on 13 July 1878' at Berlin; Montenegro's independence was formally recognised.

region.text: Niksic, Kolasin, Spuz, Podgorica, Zabljak and Bar, with sea access

ledger.note: 13 July 1878: independence recognised and the territory doubles. 'The Ottoman Empire recognized Montenegro's independence at the Treaty of Berlin'; the territory 'grew from 4,405 km2 to 9,475 km2, including Niksic, Kolasin, Spuz, Podgorica, Zabljak, Bar, and sea access' (the page ties the figures to the Treaty of San Stefano of 3 March 1878). Cliopatria draws the land from 1885; Ulcinj's handover date is not on the pages opened.
28 August 1910: the principality becomes a kingdom. 'Prince Nikola of Montenegro proclaimed the Kingdom of Montenegro in Cetinje on 28 August 1910.'

region.text: the Sanjak, Metohija and the Scutari district, the land the Cliopatria shape adds in 1912

ledger.note: 1912: Montenegro joins the First Balkan War. 'Joined the First Balkan War, hoping to gain Ottoman-held areas of Rumelia.' The page gives no month for the opening or for the Scutari siege.

region.text: the newly captured city of Shkodër (Skadar)

ledger.note: May 1913: Montenegro gives up Shkodër. 'the Montenegrins had to abandon the newly captured city of Skadar' to Albania under Great Power pressure.

region.text: its half of the Sandzak (Sanjak of Novi Pazar): Pljevlja, Bijelo Polje and Rozaje as the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 30 May 1913: Montenegro and Serbia split the Sanjak of Novi Pazar. 'Montenegro did make further territorial gains by splitting Sandzak with Serbia on 30 May 1913.'

region.text: the Sanjak, Metohija and the Scutari district

ledger.note: May 1913: the war with the Ottomans ends for Montenegro with the loss of Shkodër and the split of the Sandzak (30 May 1913); the Treaty of London is not named on the page opened.

region.text: the regions of Berane, Ipek and Gjakova (Metohija)

ledger.note: 10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest confirms Metohija. 'The treaty awarded the regions of Berane, Ipek and Gjakova (Metohija) to Montenegro.' The page does not give the previous holder, which the researcher takes to be the Ottoman Empire.

15 January 1916: Austria-Hungary occupies Montenegro. 'Austria-Hungary occupied Montenegro from 15 January 1916 to October 1918'; 'King Nikola and his government went into exile.' Written from the occupied state's side, as the Serbs dossier does; Austria-Hungary's own dossier should carry the occupier's event.
October 1918: the Austro-Hungarian occupation ends ('from 15 January 1916 to October 1918').

region.text: the Kingdom of Montenegro, united with Serbia

ledger.note: 26 November 1918: the Podgorica Assembly deposes Nikola and votes union with Serbia. 'On 26 November 1918, the Podgorica Assembly' adopted a resolution 'deposing King Nikola I'; 'On 1 December 1918, Serbia and Montenegro together formed a major part of the new' Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. The page's introduction gives 28 November for the proclamation of unification.

3 June 2006: Montenegro is independent again. The referendum was held 'on 21 May 2006' and 'On 3 June 2006, the Montenegrin Parliament declared the independence of Montenegro', ending the state union of Serbia and Montenegro (created 2003). The land is the country within its present borders.

notes:
Five pages: the principality, the Treaty of Berlin, the kingdom, the modern state and the Treaty of Bucharest (the last opened for the Greek dossier and reused). Cliopatria's single 'Montenegro' row covers two lives, 1853-1915 and 2006-2024; this dossier keeps them as one state with a merge in 1918 and a gain in 2006, and the years 1919-2005 are Yugoslavia and Serbia and Montenegro (rows of other groups). A gap-filler may prefer two dossiers. identity.successors is empty because the state is alive; the 1918 handover is the merge event with the Serbs row.

Cliopatria points proposed: the 1880-1884 shape is the pre-Berlin Montenegro (verdict wrong), the 1885 growth belongs to 1878; the 1912 shape holds Scutari, which was taken only in 1913; 1916-1918 has no shape although the kingdom lived on in exile (new keyframe). Not settled: when Ulcinj and Plav-Gusinje were settled (1880, not on the pages opened); the +237 km2 of 1911; the 1858 gains against the shape (the page text lists Niksic among the 1858 gains, which contradicts its own 1878 list, so only Grahovo and Rudine are used); the Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro (predecessor, no dossier), whose years and borders no page opened gives; the Kingdom page's date of 26 November against the introduction's 28 November for the unification. Area checks: 1853 shape 6,131 km2 against 4,405 (1.39); 1885 shape 8,794 against 9,475 (0.93); 1913 shape 14,165 against 14,000 (1.01); 2006 shape 13,931 against 13,883 (1.00).

The occupation events are written from the occupied state's side (counterpart = occupier), following the Serbs dossier; the Austro-Hungarian dossier should hold the mirror. Gazetteer: the Sandzak half is given by the municipalities Pljevlja, Bijelo Polje and Rozaje (the 'Rascia' region does not meet the Montenegrin shape); Grahovo is given by coordinates.
